A jam is one queue that friends add to while the music plays on this phone. They join from a link, in a browser or in Nexus Music. Hosting needs a jam relay: a small service you run beside your music server, which is what lets friends reach the jam from wherever they are. Joining someone else\'s jam needs none of this.
The link for %1$s is on file
The relay prints this link when it starts. It ends with a key, so treat it like a password: this phone keeps the key where it keeps your password, not in its settings file.
Paste the host link from your relay to finish.

%1$s didn\'t answer like a jam relay.
The phone wouldn\'t keep the key. Try again.

Other devices running Nexus Music, signed in to the same account and set up with the same relay, appear under Connect to a device on Now Playing. Pick one to move what you\'re playing over to it, or to steer what it\'s playing from here. While the app is closed and nothing plays, this phone isn\'t listed.
What it\'s called in the list on your other devices.
Shown while this phone is in a jam, hosting one, or steering another device.
Connected to the jam relay. The music plays on the other device.
